claims: The Artemis II mission successfully landed on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (0007 GMT April 11).
The four-person crew of the Artemis II mission completed their 10-day test flight around the moon.
The Artemis II mission marked the first crewed return from the Moon since 1972.
The splashdown time of the Artemis II mission was 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
The splashdown location of the Artemis II mission was the Pacific Ocean west of San Diego, California.
The crew of the Artemis II mission consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The crew of the Artemis II mission were reported safe and in good condition.
The re-entry of the Artemis II mission was a successful textbook re-entry.
The crew of the Artemis II mission was picked up by helicopter.
The crew of the Artemis II mission was transported to the USS John P. Murtha.
The capsule of the Artemis II mission re-entered the atmosphere at speeds around 23,800 mph.
The capsule of the Artemis II mission deployed its parachutes for a safe landing.
